description:
FILED s419 (Fable): docs/drop-census-s419-flip-gate.md family 13 — the
umbrella for the census rows that are one-row spellings with no shared
mechanism.  Each line carries its probe note; close rows INDIVIDUALLY (edit
this list), never as a batch:

1. re/subst.t:346  `ok( ! @?, ... )` — PROBED s419: `@?` IS legal perl
   (punctuation array).  PCL drops.  Family of the %SPECIAL_VARS machinery
   (#89, completed) — likely add `@?` (and audit which other punctuation
   ARRAYS beyond @-/@+ are missing).
2. op/utftaint.t:18  `any_tainted @_;` inside `sub tainted ($)` — PROBED
   s419: does NOT reproduce isolated ((@)-prototype + parenless call
   transpiles fine).  The in-file trigger is contextual; locate before
   fixing.
3. op/filetest.t:161  `sub _ { ... }` then `is(-f _, 1, ...)` — `_` defined
   as a sub while used as the stat buffer; #403-family fidelity edge.
4. op/glob.t:110  `ok <~>, '~ works';` — tilde glob via readline brackets.
5. op/utf8cache.t:70  `substr $x, 0, 1, = "\x{100}";` — 4-arg substr
   spelled with a trailing comma before `=` (legal perl).
6. op/sub_lval.t:970  `continue { ... }` in an rvalue-return context —
   torture row of the lvalue file.
7. op/sub_lval.t:1065  `{; @119797 }` — numeric array name in a bare block.
8-9. (reserved: the two rows the harvester deduplicates — same-line
   duplicate heredoc statements in comp/parser.t:733; they are counted
   under the test-deliberate family 6.)

None of these is worth a session alone; they are fillers by the s366
filler-scope rule (same mechanism + gate-SET measured + new axes filed).
Together they block the announce->DIE flip (flip-gate doc section 4).

s420 UPDATE (no rows closed here, but two of the nine are now measured):
  * item 1 (`@?`): PPI lexes `@?` as Cast(@) + Operator(?) — it is not in its
    %MAGIC table, and unlike `@-`/`@+` there is no token for it.  So this one
    needs a token repair plus an emission plus a defvar, the same three pieces
    `@#` has; it is NOT a one-line %SPECIAL_VARS addition.
  * item 4 (`<~>`): PCL crashes rather than dropping (measured s420) — the
    tilde glob reaches the runtime and dies there, so this row's cost is a
    dead FILE, not a dead statement.

s427 UPDATE (Opus): items 1 and 4 CLOSED; the other five stay open with what
was measured.

ITEM 1 (`@?`) DONE.  Two halves.  (a) PPI splits `@?` into Cast('@') +
Operator('?') — logged as docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §24 with two failing rows
in docs/ppi-bug-report.t.  Pl::Parser::_merge_punct_array_symbols merges them
back; the merge is licensed by the grammar, not by a name list: in valid perl
a `@` CAST can only be followed by `$`, `{` or an identifier, so a cast
abutting an operator is a parse of no legal program.  (b) THE OTHER HALF
NEEDED NO PPI BUG AT ALL: `$?[1]` is element 1 of `@?` and has always lowered
to `(p-aref @? 1)` through the machinery that serves `$#[0]`, but ONLY `@#`
was ever forward-declared, so a file containing `$?[…]` died at LOAD with an
unbound variable — a crash the census cannot see.  Parser2's punctuation
bucket now declares the whole family.  The BOUNDARY is the CL symbol spelling,
not perl: `? ! . / ~ ^ & % = < >` are CL constituents and read bare like `@#`;
the rest (`@,` `@;` `@|` `@'` `@"` `@(`) need a pipe-quoted spelling and are
task #449.

ITEM 4 (`<~>`) DONE, and it was three things.  perlop states the readline rule
as a WHITELIST (a filehandle, a simple scalar holding one, or empty; everything
else globs) and PCL had the inverse, a blacklist of glob metacharacters — so
`<~>` emitted `(p-readline ~)`, an unbound CL symbol, and so did `<foo.txt>`.
(a) The scalar test must allow a package QUALIFIER: Parser2's renames rewrite
the symbol inside the token, so scalar.t's `<$fh>` arrives as
`<$main::fh__file__0>` (corpus-diff caught this; perl reads `<$main::fh>` as a
readline too).  (b) After a list-operator Word PPI lexes `<~>` as three
operators (§14) and _fix_ppi_glob_after_block did not rebuild it because `~`
was not in its glob-metacharacter class — it IS one and is less ambiguous than
the `*` already there.  (c) `<<>>` (perl 5.22's double diamond) arrives as a
Readline token whose inner text is `<>`: it is named explicitly, or the
whitelist would glob the string "<>" SILENTLY (the COMPANION A/B found this,
nothing else did — io/argv.t 23/30 -> 27/26).  p-glob expands a leading tilde
now (bsd_glob's rule; an unknown user and a non-leading tilde are left alone).
Census: t/op/glob.t 1 -> 0 (row removed), t/re/subst.t 3 -> 2.
Guard Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t (11 rows, 17 s).

STILL OPEN, each measured s427:
  * item 2 (op/utftaint.t:18) — re-confirmed: does NOT reproduce isolated.
    The trigger is contextual and unlocated; locating it is a hunt.
  * item 3 (op/filetest.t:161) — #403-family; no row in the O3 batch depended
    on it.
  * item 5 (op/utf8cache.t:70, `substr $x, 0, 1, = "Z"`) — still DROPS loudly;
    perl accepts it (probed).  A term-grammar shape that leads into
    _reduce_term / the $end_pars region: B3's, not a filler's.
  * item 6 (op/sub_lval.t:970, `continue { … }`) — the lvalue file's torture
    row; that file is 33 lvalue-exempt drops already.
  * item 7 (op/sub_lval.t:1065, `{; @119797 }`) — still DROPS, and WORSE than
    one row: the drop SWALLOWS the following statement
    (`{; @119797 } print "B\n";` is one dropped statement).  Also B3-shaped.

s431 UPDATE (Opus, the P1 flip re-census â docs/drop-census-s431-flip-gate.md).
This task now owns ELEVEN census rows, because two shapes s419 filed under
"deliberate parse-error torture" were PROBED and are VALID PERL:

  * t/io/open.t:267  `ok open(...), 'desc', || _diag $!;`  â probed s431:
    perl accepts it and prints `ok(1 desc)`; PCL drops the statement.
    Minimal: `sub ok {...} sub _diag {...} ok $x, 'desc', || _diag "boom";`
  * t/op/utf8cache.t:70  `substr $x, 0, 1, = "\x{100}";` â probed s431:
    perl assigns (`Zbc`), PCL drops and prints `abc` (SILENT WRONG).
    (This was item 5 already; the s431 probe confirms it is legal perl, so it
    is a gap, not a torture row.)
  * t/comp/parser.t 432, 456, 733 x2, 764 (5 rows) â all legal perl in a file
    perl itself compiles: `"${; =pod =cut }"` (pod inside an interpolated
    block), `sub 'Hello'_he_said (_);` (the old `'` package separator), two
    heredocs on one line each carrying `${...}` interpolation, and a heredoc
    whose body contains `#line`.  s419 counted these as "deliberate parse-error
    torture rows"; only t/comp/final_line_num.t's `print 1+` is that.

Plus the three still-open s419 items that remain census rows: op/filetest.t:161
(item 3), op/sub_lval.t:970 (item 6), op/sub_lval.t:1065 (item 7).  Item 2
(op/utftaint.t) is no longer a census row.

Rows that LEFT this task in s431: t/re/pat.t:106 -> #458 (the section-11 repair
declines on a quantifier); the glob/symbolic-ref spellings -> #463.
